title: Causal-footprint masking (default ON, no off switch) can accept a net-negative candidate
evidence: Out-of-footprint paired deltas are replaced by 0.0 before the 1-SE test. Footprint = named code surfaces (def/call/"name":) on changed lines + enclosing def, matched as substrings in rollouts; prose/policy edits name no surface. Synthetic case: tool edit + prose rule breaking 6 unrelated tasks gives full-vector mean -0.067 (reject) but masked +0.133 > 1*SE 0.063 (accept) with candidate val mean lower than parent. footprint_gate has no CLI/spec switch; gate_max_broke default None and not forwarded by cap-evolve run.
impact_on_paper: The gated statistic of hill-climb/skillopt (and agent-optimize --mode paired rounds) is a masked, different statistic from the reported val curve; any claim that 'accepts imply val improvement' or comparisons of accept counts across arms is invalid unless footprint is disabled or reported. Needs an ablation arm (footprint on/off).
proposed_correction: Make footprint_gate a spec/CLI option defaulting OFF for paper runs; or compute the gate on the full vector and use the footprint only for diagnostics; always veto on resolved full-split regressions (gate_max_broke default 0 when footprint is applied); log both statistics per step.

title: Default one-SE paired gate has ~16% single-test and ~50% per-10-iteration false-accept rate; no multiplicity control
evidence: k_se=1.0 => one-sided z-test at alpha~0.159. Null simulation (same true rates): single-test accept 0.15-0.17 (T=30..140, 1..5 trials); P(>=1 false accept in 10 sequential null candidates) 0.51-0.58. Docs (gate.py header, hill-climb SKILL.md) present it as what 'makes an accept mean something'. act.judge docstring itself cites 39% cumulative false-accept over 8 looks.
impact_on_paper: Reported 'accepted improvements' include noise ratchets; val gains need a null-candidate (no-op) control arm to be interpretable. Do not describe the gate as statistically valid at 5%.
proposed_correction: Document as heuristic; expose k_se in paper configs with a null-edit control; consider Bonferroni/alpha-spending over iterations, or accept only after fresh-trial confirmation; add simulated null calibration test to the suite.

title: Val is both the proposer's feedback source and the acceptance split (adaptive reuse); train unused by hill-climb and agent-optimize
evidence: run_step injects the parent's VAL trajectories and per-task val rows and gates on val; hill_climb_loop focus order is read_splits().val; agent-optimize runs diagnose --split val and reads val exemplar traces. Train is evaluated only at baseline/finalize bookends. Only the sealed test is unadaptive.
impact_on_paper: Val curves, best_val, stop_at_reward and any 'val improvement' are selection-biased (winner's curse); the paper must report test (or fresh-seed holdout) deltas as the primary result and label val as development data. GEPA (train minibatch reflection) is structurally different from hill-climb/agent-optimize in this respect.
proposed_correction: Add an optional train-reflection / val-gate split for hill-climb and agent-optimize (proposer sees train only); at minimum report val-vs-test gap per run and describe val as adaptive.

title: Coverage guard is candidate-marginal; errored trials silently dropped from the pair, so candidate-induced crashes can be invisible
evidence: min_coverage=0.6 hard-coded (not in CLI/spec). run_step passes candidate coverage only; gate_check passes min(marginal_cand, marginal_ref). Joint paired coverage is never checked: marginals 0.70/0.70 with joint n=12/30 still judged. Errored trials are excluded from mean and pair, so a candidate that crashes on 6 tasks the parent passes (paired n=24) is accepted (Δ̄=+0.167>SE 0.078, val 0.733->0.833). trials.py turns ANY exception in run_one into an error rollout (dropped).
impact_on_paper: Candidate-caused failures coded as 'errored' inflate val and acceptance; coverage should be reported per run and accept counts conditioned on joint coverage. Affects reliability of any adapter that raises on bad candidate code.
proposed_correction: Gate on joint paired coverage (valid in both) with a configurable min_coverage; treat errored trials in the candidate arm as failures unless the adapter marks infra explicitly with a reason code; expose min_coverage in spec; report n_dropped_pairs.

title: Fresh-trial 'confirmation' in agent-optimize finalize pools selection-era trials with the new ones
evidence: finalize tops up the champion's SAME tag by n_confirm=3 trials and calls judge(champion,'seed'); gate_check loads ALL rollouts of that tag via objectives.load_trials, i.e. the trials that drove promotion plus the 3 fresh ones, vs seed baseline val rollouts. Digest p_beat additionally pools by cap_hash across tags (ledger), a different pool.
reproduction: read act.py:524-531 + gate_check.py:260-263 (static); no run required
impact_on_paper: The confirm step is not an independent replication: winner's-curse bias is diluted not removed; a 'confirmed' champion may still fail on genuinely fresh trials (cf. campaign #744 failed full-val confirmation of a merged candidate).
proposed_correction: Gate the confirm on fresh trials only (separate tag/trial_idx range) or report both pooled and fresh-only statistics; require fresh-only z above the same bar before sealing.

title: reward_gated promote gate has a hard-coded SE floor (0.031) that sets a ~0.085 minimum accepted effect at any sample size; sequential-validity claim not enforced
evidence: NOISE_FLOOR=0.031 was measured on run_20261008_150326 and applied to all splits. z_accept=2.734 (alpha 0.05/(2*8)). se=max(sd/sqrt(n),0.031) => dR must exceed ~0.085 regardless of n_tasks/trials. Simulation: P(accept | true +0.05)=0.5-10% and P(accept | +0.10)=10-39% for T=30-140, 3-8 trials; power at T=140 does NOT increase with trials. 'looks=8' is a constant: no per-candidate look counter and no multiplicity across candidates, though the docstring says the false-accept rate is <= alpha.
impact_on_paper: agent-optimize is structurally unable to promote moderate real gains (<~9 points); null results or failed confirmations may reflect the floor rather than the optimizer. Any 'agent-optimize beats X' or 'no gain' claim needs the MDE stated.
proposed_correction: Make noise_floor a measured per-run quantity (from byte-identical repeat cells, which digest already estimates) or default 0; enforce a look counter per candidate; add a cross-candidate correction or document the family-wise rate.

title: Test seal is per run directory; --reuse-baseline resets it, so a campaign repeatedly consumes the same held-out split
evidence: test_used lives in each run's splits.json; reuse_baseline copies the frozen split and forces test_used=False and carries the seed's test result forward; make_splits(seed) is deterministic. No cross-run ledger/warning. evaluate_candidate(split='test') is callable outside finalize (open #361); CAPEVOLVE_ALLOW_TEST_RESCORE=1 overrides the second-look guard.
reproduction: static (reuse_baseline body); or run baseline twice with same seed and compare splits.json
impact_on_paper: If the paper runs many arms/configs on the same test split and reports/selects the best, the test set is no longer a single unadaptive look. The paper must either use per-arm disjoint test splits, a campaign-level test ledger, or state the multiplicity.
proposed_correction: Add a campaign-level seal (hash of test ids -> usage ledger) that warns/refuses on reuse across runs, and disclose reuse in final.json. Overlaps #361/#335 (see notes).

title: Optimizer subprocess is not isolated from the adapter/scorer/benchmark; integrity seal hashes only the candidate workdir and is OFF by default; agent-optimize has no seal
evidence: snapshot() is taken on work/<cid> after context injection; project/adapter.py and scorer.py live outside it. A subprocess run through the real optimizer_from_command rewrote project/scorer.py and verify().ok stayed True; manifest covered no files. Optimizer inherits os.environ (provider keys). CLI grants Bash / --dangerously-skip-permissions / --yolo. The Claude hook matches Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit only. agent-optimize scripts reference neither protected_paths nor integrity, yet SKILL.md says core enforces 'the tamper guard'.
impact_on_paper: DUPLICATE of #276 (open) and #365 (meta); the agent-optimize 'no seal' + false SKILL claim is new (see issue draft D08). Scorer tampering cannot be excluded for any run in the paper; claims of 'honest evaluation' must say runs relied on optimizer good behavior.
proposed_correction: Run optimizer in a sandbox with read-only project/scorer mounts and scrubbed env; hash the project eval surface (adapter, scorer, tasks) rather than the workdir; wire integrity into agent-optimize's promote/finalize; correct SKILL.md.

title: commit.py --decision accept performs no gate check; accept is coupled to a gate only by convention (act.py promote)
evidence: set_best executes for accepted=True with only a --val==measured-mean check; reject paths have extensive gate attribution checks but accept has none. act.prune passes five justification flags automatically.
impact_on_paper: In agent mode an accepted champion is whatever the driving agent booked; the paper should treat only act.py promote accepts (gate_mode field in events) as gated.
proposed_correction: Require a recorded passing gate_check/judge row for decision accept (or --accept-without-gate REASON).

title: agent-optimize requires switches that are OFF by default (active_eval); behaviour and posterior rule depend on configuration; docs call posterior 'sequentially valid' but it is not the default accept rule
evidence: DEFAULTS: active_eval=False, cost_gating=True. With stock defaults probe --auto runs full val and promote uses reward_gated, not the posterior. Posterior used for display/allocation only unless cost_gating is off. My simulation supports low null false-accept (1.6-3.6%, N=250 per cell) for a single fixed pair, but the guarantee does not cover multiple candidates, merges, adaptive proposals, or generalization (D is a finite-val-set quantity); constants are hand-set.
impact_on_paper: Paper must specify the ablation vector per run; 'agent-optimize' results with and without active_eval are different algorithms.
proposed_correction: Ship the documented engine as the default or version the algorithm name; qualify 'sequentially valid' in comments.

title: stats.combined_stderr double-counts within-task trial variance and does not shrink with trials
evidence: SE^2 = var_between/n + sum(se_i^2)/n^2, but var_between already contains the within-task noise. Fixed-val re-measurement sd 0.054/0.034/0.027/0.019 at 1/3/5/10 trials vs combined_stderr 0.080/0.069/0.065/0.057 (1.5x-3.0x).
impact_on_paper: Reported 'val +- se', final.json, significant-mode, convergence and any noise comparison are inflated and trial-insensitive; the default paired gate does not use it.
proposed_correction: Use a stated estimand: for a fixed task set, SE = sqrt(sum se_i^2)/n; for task-population inference, use the between-task sample variance only. Document which.

title: Bundled GEPA is not official GEPA: extra significance gate before pool admission, agent-CLI proposer, fixed-seed single-draw cached minibatch
evidence: Official engine evaluates every minibatch-improved proposal on the full valset and adds it to the pool unconditionally (best by val aggregate). Bundled: pool admission requires paired 1-SE gate (rejected candidates never join the frontier). Minibatch size 4 vs official 3; eval cache keyed (cap_hash, task) only; fixed seed; footprint not used in GEPA gate.
impact_on_paper: Any 'GEPA' baseline from this repo must be labelled 'cap-evolve GEPA-style'; official GEPA baselines (campaign #742) are needed for fair comparison.
proposed_correction: Add an --official-admission mode (admit all minibatch-improved) and an LLM-call proposer; key cache on seed/model/adapter version.

title: Bundled SkillOpt: mini-batch focus is empty, acceptance is not 'strictly improves held-out val', edit budget advisory
evidence: Train mini-batch ids are intersected with val rows -> empty focus (open #371, #382, #395); each step evaluates full val and uses the paired 1-SE gate + footprint.

title: Issue #351 (one-task gain: delta==SE) is closed but still reproduces; SKILL.md says 'open'
evidence: decide(paired, k=1, deltas=[1]+[0]*(n-1)): n=4 reject, 8 reject, 20 ACCEPT, 30 reject, 40 ACCEPT, 60 reject (float rounding).
reproduction: cd /tmp && python3.12 -I -c "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'core');from cap_evolve import gate;print([gate.decide(0.5,0.5,mode='paired',paired_deltas=[1.0]+[0.0]*(n-1),k_se=1.0).accept for n in (4,8,20,30,40,60)])"
impact_on_paper: Acceptance of single-task gains is arbitrary; affects small-val benchmarks.
proposed_correction: Reopen #351 or fix the comparison (explicit tolerance / documented tie rule).

title: Documentation line references and claims drifted from code (hill-climb SKILL.md cites harness.py:1409 etc.; agent-optimize SKILL claims tamper guard)
evidence: run_step is at harness.py:2818 (docs: 1409); gate.py cites harness.py:1524-1526 for paired selection (actual 3005-3006).
